subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: Should OpenClaw adopt persisted provider-level cooldown identity for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including the `inline-api-key:<provider>` usage namespace and fail-closed availability behavior during auth/billing windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but the fix changes auth-provider availability and recovery behavior for existing inline-key users, so final acceptance needs maintainer product and compatibility intent after the mechanical blocker is repaired.

options.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
options.body: Land this direction after the remaining availability call-site repair so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable.

options.title: Keep cooldowns profile-only
options.body: Decline this PR direction and document auth profiles as the supported workaround for users who need cooldown protection.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers specify exact persistence, recovery, and UI visibility behavior for inline provider cooldown state.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level inline cooldown
recommendation.body: Land this direction after the remaining availability call-site repair so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest history match for the model auth/profile boundary and the SecretRef auth behavior changed here.
